extracted.intended_audience: NIH extramural researchers, grant applicants, research administrators, and institutional research offices
extracted.subtask_description: A news/index page summarizing recent NIH extramural policy, process, and resource updates relevant to grant applicants and administrators. Contains short summaries linking to guidance on application formats, data management, review procedures, and program changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selecting appropriate models (New Approach Methodologies - NAMs)
rubrics_metrics.description: "Investigators should still select the models most appropriate for their specific research questions."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NIH supports a wide range of scientifically sound approaches and encourages approaches that enhance human relevance and translational potential. Choose models that best address the specific hypothesis and research question rather than defaulting to a particular system; consider human relevance and translational potential when justifying model choice.

rubrics_metrics.name: PF5 Collaborative International Research Projects: application format and linked awards
rubrics_metrics.description: "Watch NIH’s 6-minute overview of the new Collaborative International Research Project (PF5) award structure to learn key features, application format, and how applications may be split into linked awards after review and before Just-in-Time requests."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the specified PF5 application format precisely. Be aware that applications may be administratively split into linked awards after peer review and prior to Just-in-Time (JIT) requests; plan research scope and budgets accordingly and watch NIH overview materials for key features.

rubrics_metrics.name: 2026 Pilot Data Management and Sharing (DMS) Plan format and required elements
rubrics_metrics.description: "We have issued a new 2026 Pilot DMS Plan format based on a simplified set of required elements to use when preparing Data Management and Sharing (DMS) Plans."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the 2026 Pilot DMS Plan format when preparing DMS plans for applicable applications. Include the simplified set of required elements specified in the pilot format; consult the issued resource for the exact elements and examples to ensure compliance with NIH data sharing expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expectation to embed replication and reproducibility
rubrics_metrics.description: “The reliability of biomedical research is foundational to public trust in science and to ensuring that findings can benefit patients and communities. NIH’s Gold Standard Science plan advances this commitment by encouraging a culture that values replication and reproducibility. In support of this plan, NIH has launched a new Replication and Reproducibility Initiative to drive, incentivize and institutionalize replication and reproducibility efforts across the biomedical research enterprise.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should explicitly address replication and reproducibility in applications and study design where relevant. NIH is highlighting replication/reproducibility as a topic and creating incentives; consider including plans for validation, replication, transparent methods, and practices that enhance reliability to align with NIH priorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scoring designation: "Competitive But Not Discussed" (CBND) and 33% cut-off context
rubrics_metrics.description: “Recognizing that strong applications may fall below a 33% cut off, the middle third of applications in a study section were designated as ‘competitive but not discussed.’”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Understand that NIH implemented emergency modifications such that the middle third of applications in a study section could be scored as 'competitive but not discussed' (CBND). This affects expectations about discussion and triage; a CBND designation indicates competitiveness but the application may not have been discussed in full panel review. Applicants should monitor notices explaining how score cutoffs and triage policies are applied.

rubrics_metrics.name: Centralized NIH peer review within the Center for Scientific Review (CSR)
rubrics_metrics.description: “In March 2025, NIH announced that all peer review would be centralized within the Center for Scientific Review (CSR).”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Peer review consolidation aims to strengthen efficiency, competition, and transparency. Applicants should note that review processes, study section assignments, and administrative practices are centralized within CSR; consult CSR guidance and NIH notices for any procedural or timeline changes that may affect submission strategy and expectations.
